Evidence:

- Every process creates an isolated in-memory backend: `cmd/lostpet-service/main.go:18-20`, `cmd/foundpet-service/main.go:19-22`, `cmd/pet-matcher/main.go:16-18`, `cmd/notification-service/main.go:13-15`, `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:31-34`.

- Only memory implementations exist in `pkg/store/store.go:25-109`, `pkg/pubsub/pubsub.go:22-62`, and `pkg/blob/blob.go:31-100`.

Suggested issue: `feat(runtime): implement one durable shared report-to-match path`

Acceptance criteria:

- Implement Firestore state and GCS blob adapters using ADC.
- Define canonical collections and production data models.
- Production startup must reject memory adapters.
- Remove automatic demo seeding and hard-coded candidate IDs from production mode.
- Run Firestore/Pub/Sub/storage emulators or equivalent shared local dependencies in Compose.
- Prove a report survives service restart and is visible to another process.
- Add an emulator-backed and deployed smoke test for one vertical cascade.

Dependencies/duplicates: closed #3, #23, #90, and #93 are stale or only implemented interfaces/UI wiring; #66 is infrastructure-only.

### P0 — Pub/Sub and the Cloud Run worker model do not work

Evidence:

- Each binary owns a separate `MemoryPubSub`, so publishers cannot reach subscribers across containers.
- OpenTofu creates topics only, with no subscriptions: `infra/opentofu/modules/pubsub/main.tf:1-11`.
- `pet-matcher` and `notification-service` never listen on `$PORT`: `cmd/pet-matcher/main.go:15-31`, `cmd/notification-service/main.go:13-26`.
- Both are nevertheless declared as Knative Cloud Run Services: `deploy/cloudrun/pet-matcher.yaml:1-18`, `deploy/cloudrun/notification-service.yaml:1-18`.

A Cloud Run Service ingress container must listen on its injected port. Google also recommends Pub/Sub push for Cloud Run services; pull-based workloads should deliberately use a worker pool instead. [Cloud Run container contract](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/container-contract), [Cloud Run autoscaling](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/about-instance-autoscaling), [subscription types](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/subscription-overview).

Suggested issue: `feat(pubsub): add authenticated Cloud Run push consumers`

Acceptance criteria:

- Add real Pub/Sub publishers and one subscription per consumer.
- Prefer authenticated push endpoints for matcher and notification handlers; otherwise document and provision worker pools.
- Grant the Pub/Sub push identity only `run.invoker` on its target.
- Return 2xx only after successful processing; temporary failures must produce redelivery.
- Provision ack/retry/retention/DLQ settings and DLQ subscriptions in OpenTofu.
- Verify authenticated delivery, redelivery, poison-message handling, and emulator/local behavior.

Dependencies/duplicates: #91 overlaps retry/DLQ but does not solve the missing transport or invalid Cloud Run execution model; its implementation proposal should be rewritten around subscription policy. Closed #22 promised subscriptions but created only topics.

### P0 — “Completed” GCS upload support is still a mock

Evidence:

- The upload handler constructs `MemoryBlobStore` per request: `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:772-795`.
- The generated URL contains literal `sig=mock-sig`: `pkg/blob/blob.go:75-99`.
- `foundpet-service` reserves but never uses the blob dependency: `cmd/foundpet-service/service.go:14-27`.
- The storage bucket has no CORS or explicit public-access-prevention policy: `infra/opentofu/modules/storage/main.tf:1-9`.

Suggested action: reopen stale closed issue #62 rather than file a duplicate.

Additional acceptance criteria:

- Generate GCS V4 signed uploads with bounded object prefix, content type, size, and expiry.
- Verify object metadata before creating a found-pet record.
- Enforce bucket public-access prevention; signed URLs remain compatible with it.
- Restrict CORS to configured frontend origins and required methods/headers.
- Add orphan-upload cleanup and emulator/integration coverage.

Relevant guidance: [public access prevention and signed URLs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/public-access-prevention), [Cloud Storage CORS](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/cross-origin).

### P0 — Authentication closure is stale; production exposure would expose mutations

Evidence:

- Routes are registered without authentication middleware at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:47-71`.
- Anyone can confirm/reject matches at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:576-618`, send a purported “secure” contact message at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:626-652`, or mark a pet reunited at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:661-699`.

Evidence:

- The client defaults to `http://localhost:11434`: `pkg/ollama/client.go:16`, `pkg/ollama/client.go:45-56`.
- The matcher manifest supplies no `OLLAMA_HOST`, model service, authentication, or GPU, and allocates only 2 CPU/2 GiB: `deploy/cloudrun/pet-matcher.yaml:9-18`.
- OpenTofu has no model-serving resource: `infra/opentofu/main.tf:16-39`.

Suggested issue: `feat(ai): provision private Gemma 4 inference for production`

Acceptance criteria:

- Record an architecture decision: private Cloud Run GPU Ollama versus managed Vertex AI.
- If retaining Ollama, provision an authenticated internal GPU Cloud Run service, set `OLLAMA_HOST`, model loading/startup probes, request timeout, concurrency, maximum instances, and quota.
- Do not expose Ollama publicly.
- Benchmark representative images for quality, p50/p95 latency, cold start, throughput, and cost.
- Add circuit breaking, bounded retries, and a user-visible deferred/retry state.
- Add model/version provenance to results.

Google now documents Gemma 4/Ollama on GPU Cloud Run, but it requires materially different resources and explicit cost/concurrency controls. - `Dockerfile:8` sends the entire repository into the build context, and there is no `.dockerignore`.
- GitHub currently has zero environments, Actions secrets, and variables.

- Authenticate GitHub using Workload Identity Federation, never a service-account key.

### P1 — Least-privilege identity and ingress are absent

Evidence:

- Cloud Run resources specify only name, location, and image: `infra/opentofu/modules/cloudrun/main.tf:1-54`.
- No user-managed service accounts, IAM bindings, invoker policies, or ingress settings exist.
- Outputs call every service URL “Public”: `infra/opentofu/outputs.tf:1-24`.

Suggested action: expand/retitle open #66 to `feat(infra): enforce service identities and Cloud Run ingress`.

Acceptance criteria:

- Dedicated service account per service.
- Resource-scoped Firestore, Storage, Pub/Sub, Secret Manager, and invoker roles.
- Only the intended browser entrypoint is unauthenticated.
- Matcher/notification endpoints accept only authenticated Pub/Sub delivery.
- Decide whether public traffic uses direct `run.app` or an external load balancer; if the latter, disable direct public ingress and add Armor/rate-limiting policy.
- Avoid the Compute Engine default service account.

Google recommends user-managed identities with minimal roles and layered ingress plus IAM. [Cloud Run service identity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/securing/service-identity), [Cloud Run ingress](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/securing/ingress).

Evidence:

- No backend block or environment structure exists: `infra/opentofu/main.tf:1-39`.

Acceptance criteria:

- Bootstrap a private, versioned, access-controlled GCS state bucket.
- Commit the dependency lock file and pin intentionally reviewed provider ranges.

### P1 — Data protection, indexes, and disaster recovery are undefined

Evidence:

- Firestore is a bare regional database: `infra/opentofu/modules/firestore/main.tf:1-5`.
- No PITR, scheduled backup, deletion protection, TTL, or indexes exist.
- The bucket sets `force_destroy = true`: `infra/opentofu/modules/storage/main.tf:1-9`.

- The region defaults to `us-central1` with no availability/RPO decision: `infra/opentofu/variables.tf:6-10`.

Suggested issue: `feat(data): define RPO, backups, indexes, and restore drills`

- Set production deletion protection, PITR, and scheduled backups.
- Declare every required composite/geospatial/query index in code.

- Reliably publish outbox records and track completion.

- Add crash-point and redelivery tests.

- Production fails fast on missing bucket/topic/endpoint/provider config.

## Outcome

PetSpotR is currently a polished in-memory demo, not yet a functioning multi-process local application or production-ready GCP system.

I audited `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`, reconciled open and closed issues, reviewed local development, GCP infrastructure, product behavior, security boundaries, CI/CD, and filed 23 net-new issues: [#107–#129](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20is%3Aopen%20label%3Aagent-found).

### The fundamental blocker

Every executable creates its own `MemoryStore` and `MemoryPubSub`. Consequently:

- Reports submitted through the browser never reach the report services.
- Events cannot cross Compose containers.
- State disappears on restart.
- The matcher and notification worker cannot receive another process’s events.
- Local and Cloud Run deployments cannot produce the documented cascade.

The web frontend also maintains duplicate APIs and different collection names, while the matcher uses a hardcoded lost-pet ID, hardcoded traits, and fake matches seeded on reads.

### GCP blockers

- Matcher and notification are declared as Cloud Run Services but never listen on `$PORT`, violating the [Cloud Run container contract](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/container-contract).
- Pub/Sub infrastructure creates topics but no subscriptions, authenticated push identities, retries, or DLQs. Cloud Run services should generally use authenticated [Pub/Sub push delivery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/authenticate-push-subscriptions), unless worker pools are chosen deliberately.
- GCS uploads are mocks containing `sig=mock-sig`.
- Firestore has no production adapters, indexes, PITR/backups, deletion protection, or restore process.
- No service identities, least-privilege IAM, ingress policy, Secret Manager integration, remote OpenTofu state, environment separation, or declarative API enablement exists.
- Deployment uses mutable `gcr.io/...:latest` images with no CD workflow. New delivery should use Artifact Registry and immutable digests; Google documents the [Container Registry transition](https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/transition/transition-from-gcr).
- Production inference is undefined. Matcher defaults to local Ollama, while its Cloud Run configuration has no model endpoint or GPU. Cloud Run GPU inference needs materially different resource, concurrency, quota, and cost decisions under the [GPU requirements](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/gpu).

### Product and security blockers

- Report schemas discard most entered pet, image, custody, and contact fields.
- Lost-pet listing can return reporter email.
- Match/contact/reunion mutations are unauthenticated and report success for nonexistent or unperformed work.
- Matcher passes an image URL to Ollama where validated image bytes/base64 are required.
- `/pets` is linked throughout the UI but returns 404.
- Filtering and pagination are nondeterministic or silently ineffective.
- Match rendering interpolates persisted fields into `innerHTML`, creating a stored DOM-injection path once real user data reaches matches.
- Public upload, inference, notification, and contact endpoints have no abuse controls.
- Accessibility gaps include missing mobile navigation, mouse-only uploads, inaccessible dialogs, and absent focus/reduced-motion handling.
- Public claims such as 98.4% accuracy, sub-three-second matching, and operational success are unsupported by real evaluation or infrastructure.

## Filed backlog

The recommended implementation order is:

1. Runtime and contracts: [#107](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/107), [#113](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/113), [#114](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/114).
2. Identity and safe ingestion: [#109](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/109), [#110](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/110), [#128](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/128), [#129](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/129).
3. Event delivery and local emulators: [#108](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/108), [#116](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/116), [#117](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/117).
4. Real matching and inference: [#123](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/123), [#111](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/111), [#115](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/115).
5. Infrastructure and delivery: [#118](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/118), [#120](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/120), [#112](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/112).
6. Reliability and operations: [#119](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/119), [#121](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/121), [#122](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/122).
7. Product completion: [#124](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/124), [#125](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/125), [#126](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/126), [#127](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/127).

Existing #64, #65, #66, #91, and #94 remain relevant, but need the new runtime work as prerequisites. Numerous closed issues—including #3, #11, #13, #22, #23, #51–#63, #90, #92, and #93—were only partially completed; the new issues capture their remaining work as smaller verifiable slices.

## Verification and limitations

- `go test ./...` passed using Go 1.26.5.
- Docker Compose configuration validates, with only the obsolete top-level `version` warning.
- The worktree remains clean and synchronized with `origin/main`.
- No source files or infrastructure state were changed.
- OpenTofu validation was not run because `tofu` is not installed locally.
- No actual GCP project was inspected, so this assesses repository readiness rather than current deployed resources.
- The independent deep-security scanner failed to return after bounded retries. The two security issues filed were manually validated, but this should not be represented as a completed formal deep-security scan.

The best first implementation slice is [#107](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/107): introduce the durable runtime adapter selection and prove one report can cross process boundaries and survive restart.
